working_title: The evening routine that was really a work problem

exercise.instructions: You are going to read an article about changing evening routines. Six sentences have been removed from the article. Choose from the sentences A–G the one which fits each gap (37)–(42). There is one extra sentence which you do not need to use.
exercise.text_title: The evening routine that was really a work problem
exercise.passage_with_gaps:
I used to believe that a perfect evening routine was the key to feeling refreshed in the morning. Every night, I would meticulously plan activities like reading, meditating, and listening to calming music. However, even after all that effort, I still felt exhausted the next day. (37) 

Initially, I thought the solution was to change my bedtime habits. I tried everything from herbal teas to gentle yoga stretches. (38) I found myself mentally going over unfinished tasks from the day. 

One evening, while attempting to enjoy a quiet dinner, I received a message about an urgent work issue. (39) It dawned on me that my workday never truly ended, and this was why I felt so mentally occupied. 

Determined to change this, I decided to introduce a simple ritual to mark the end of my workday. I would write down the first task for the next day and physically put away my work materials. (40) 

At first, I was tempted to break this new rule. The lure of checking emails or making a quick work call was strong. (41) 

Gradually, I noticed a shift. My evenings began to feel more relaxed, and my attention turned to personal activities without the constant pull of work. (42) I realised that the real change was not about finding the perfect evening routine but about creating a clear boundary between work and personal time.

sentence_pool.A: But each time I resisted, I felt a sense of accomplishment.
sentence_pool.B: That was when I realised my evenings were not truly my own.
sentence_pool.C: Despite these changes, my mind was still occupied with work.
sentence_pool.D: This small act helped me mentally separate work from home.
sentence_pool.E: I had assumed that changing my bedtime would solve everything.
sentence_pool.F: The interruption was a clear sign that my work had no defined end.
sentence_pool.G: In the end, the boundary I created was more valuable than any routine.

questions.rationale: The sentence before the gap describes the narrator's belief in a perfect evening routine, and sentence E contrasts this by suggesting an assumption about bedtime was incorrect.
The narrator describes trying different bedtime habits, but sentence C explains the effect that these changes did not resolve the underlying issue of work occupying their mind.
The message about an urgent work issue is the interruption that reveals the lack of a defined end to the workday, which is explained in sentence F.
The narrator describes a new ritual to end the workday, and sentence D follows logically by explaining how this act helps separate work from home.
The paragraph describes the temptation to break the new rule, and sentence A contrasts this by showing the positive outcome of resisting that temptation.
The paragraph describes the shift in evening experience, and sentence G reflects on the value of the boundary created, contrasting it with the initial focus on routine.
